qt: to the Commission Stanislav Stoyanov (ESN) Subject:
Drivers holding a Category C or BE licence towing trailers weighing over 750 kg with motorhomes weighing over 3 500 kg.

Under Directive (EU) 2025/2205, a driver holding a Category C or BE licence must obtain a Category C1E or CE licence to tow a trailer weighing more than 750 kg with a motor home weighing more than 3 500 kg, even where the combined mass does not exceed 7 000 kg. This category of driver has already demonstrated the ability to drive a vehicle weighing over 3 500 kg (category C) and to tow a trailer weighing up to 3 500 kg (category BE), as well as having Group 2 medical fitness. In some Member States, drivers who obtained their licences under previous national categories have been driving such vehicles legally for decades. The weight of the combination is also limited by the motorhome’s registration documents. 1.
Does the Commission have road safety data to support the requirement for a C1E or CE licence for drivers holding C and BE licences to tow such combinations up to a maximum mass of 7 000 kg?
Was this case addressed in the impact assessment SWD(2023) 128?

Will the Commission, in its assessment under Article 24 of the Directive, consider a provision allowing holders of a Category C or C1 licence and a Category BE licence to tow such combinations up to 7 000 kg?
